title: RC charge or discharge after a voltage step
description: Calculate a capacitor's arbitrary-initial-condition step trajectory, relative-error settling time, stored energy, and accumulated resistor pulse energy.
formula: tau=RC; vC=Vs+(V0-Vs)exp(-t/tau); iC=(Vs-vC)/R; t_settle=-tau ln(epsilon); EC=C vC^2/2; ER=C(Vs-V0)^2[1-exp(-2t/tau)]/2
assumptions: Ideal constant capacitance and positive series resistance driven by an ideal constant voltage after t=0; R includes source resistance and capacitor ESR where their lumped approximation is valid.
Positive current flows from source into capacitor. Vs=0 describes discharge; no separate inverse calculator is counted.

Settling tolerance is a fraction of the initial-to-final voltage difference, not an ADC or digital threshold specification. For V0=Vs there is no transient and the reported normalized settling time is a conventional time-scale metric only.
Stored energy excludes dielectric loss; resistor pulse energy does not establish a resistor pulse-rating or safety certification.

Voltage increments and accumulated resistive energy use expm1 so arbitrarily short positive elapsed times do not lose the exponential difference to subtraction; adding a tiny increment to a nonzero initial voltage remains subject to ordinary floating-point resolution.

references.title: MIT 6.200: Optional Review, RC Circuit Derivations and Key Values
Georgia State University HyperPhysics: Energy Stored on a Capacitor

outputs.label: Resistor energy accumulated by time t

title: Unbuffered two-stage RC ladder startup
description: Compute both capacitor-node voltages and the downstream capacitor current in a passive two-stage RC ladder, retaining interstage loading instead of multiplying independent RC step responses.
formula: a=R1R2C1C2; b=R1C1+R1C2+R2C2; tau_s=(b+sqrt(b^2-4a))/2; tau_f=a/tau_s; v2=Vs[1-(tau_s exp(-t/tau_s)-tau_f exp(-t/tau_f))/(tau_s-tau_f)]; v1=v2+R2 C2 dv2/dt
assumptions: Topology: ideal source, R1, node one, R2, node two in sequence; C1 and C2 connect their respective nodes to common ground. Both capacitors initially uncharged; no external output load or buffer.
All four components are positive and linear. R1 incorporates source resistance; parasitic inductance, capacitor ESR and leakage are neglected.
The R1C2 cross term explicitly accounts for downstream loading. This is a startup transient calculation, not cutoff or filter synthesis.

The relative discriminant must be at least 1e-8 for distinct-pole numerical conditioning. The fast time constant is evaluated as a/tau_s to avoid subtracting nearly equal b and sqrt(discriminant). The shared Rust step_overdamped(t,1/tau_s,1/tau_f) primitive evaluates the same normalized analytic two-real-pole step with stable short-time conditioning; no additional time exclusion or seed output is used.

references.title: Harvey Mudd College Matthew Spencer: Review of Linear Circuits and Dynamics, KCL and step-response methods
MIT D. Rowell: Review of First- and Second-Order System Response, overdamped characteristic step response

constraints.message: Distinct modal time constants require a relative discriminant of at least 1e-8.

title: Underdamped series-RLC step ringing and peak stress
description: Predict capacitor voltage, series current, first voltage overshoot and a conservative error-envelope settling bound following a source step in an initially unenergized series RLC circuit.
formula: alpha=R/(2L); wn=1/sqrt(LC); zeta=alpha/wn; wd=sqrt(wn^2-alpha^2); vC=Vs{1-exp(-alpha t)[cos(wd t)+(alpha/wd)sin(wd t)]}; i=Vs exp(-alpha t)sin(wd t)/(L wd); tp=pi/wd; Mp=exp(-alpha pi/wd)
assumptions: Series RLC with output across C, zero initial capacitor voltage and zero initial inductor current; positive source step.
Linear unsaturated L and linear C; R is total series resistance including source resistance, winding resistance and ESR where the series lumped model holds.
Only the underdamped domain is implemented: (R/(2L))^2 must be at most (1-1e-8)/(LC). Critical and overdamped responses are not approximated by this expression.

Settling output is a sufficient envelope bound, not the exact last threshold crossing: absolute normalized voltage error <= exp(-alpha t)/sqrt(1-zeta^2). No AC resonance, Q or filter synthesis outputs are counted.
Distributed parasitics, nonlinear clamps and component pulse/voltage ratings require separate checks.

The shared Rust step_underdamped(omega_n*time,damping_ratio) primitive evaluates the same normalized analytic step with stable short-time conditioning. Its first argument is dimensionless natural-frequency time, not damped-frequency time or elapsed seconds; no additional short-time exclusion or user-facing seed output is introduced.

references.title: MIT 2.003 Prelab 5: Series RLC step response and winding-resistance correction
MIT D. Rowell: Review of First- and Second-Order System Response, underdamped roots and characteristic step response

outputs.label: First overshoot relative to final voltage

constraints.message: Circuit must be underdamped with a relative squared-frequency margin of at least 1e-8.

title: Periodic RC charging extrema under two-level excitation
description: Find periodic steady-state capacitor extrema and ripple for alternating source levels with arbitrary high and low durations, including incomplete charging memory between pulses.
formula: a=exp(-Th/RC); b=exp(-Tl/RC); Vmin=[Vl(1-b)+b Vh(1-a)]/(1-ab); Vmax=Vmin+(Vh-Vmin)(1-a); Vavg=(VhTh+VlTl)/(Th+Tl)
assumptions: An ideal voltage source switches between Vhigh and Vlow through one unchanged positive R into one linear capacitor; no DC load.
Periodic steady state is assumed, not the first pulse after startup. Vhigh>=Vlow defines extrema; source levels can be signed.
No frequency-domain filter synthesis, digital threshold, transistor switching loss or converter sizing is included.

Both pulse durations divided by RC must be at least 1e-7, retaining the researched conservative numerical domain. Exponential differences use expm1; ripple and edge currents are evaluated directly from the source-level difference rather than subtracting rounded absolute capacitor voltages.
